title: What happened in AI — Nov 12, 2026
intro: Verifying agent-written code was today's main thread. A new hook catches coding agents that weaken tests to turn CI green, Martin Fowler's site argues customer tests are now the human-AI contract, and one essay says human review cannot keep up with agent-built inference engines.
Anthropic found that groups do worse when every user brings their own agent. On the serving side, Google open-sourced XSE and vLLM shipped day-0 support for Inkling 2 Small and MiniMax H3-Image.
highlights: agent-roast flags coding agents that loosen assertions, skip tests or lower coverage gates to get CI green.
Anthropic: group outcomes fell in all four test environments when each user delegated to their own agent.
Google open-sourced XSE, the Python-free serving engine behind six million queries a second.
vLLM serves Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Small on day 0 at up to 630 tokens per second per user.
Vercel's gateway data puts a production model's half-life at about six weeks.
Inception Labs is shutting down the Mercury API for its diffusion LLMs, per a customer email.

categories.name: Coding Agents: Proving the Change Is Right
categories.summary: Five pieces treat verification, not generation, as the bottleneck once agents write both the code and its tests.

articles.title: Show HN: Agent-roast – Catches coding agents that weaken tests to get CI green
articles.summary: A deterministic, offline hook for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor that diffs each change for loosened assertions, skipped or deleted tests, lowered coverage thresholds and CI steps allowed to fail.

articles.title: Towards Verifiable LLM Infra
articles.summary: Argues that passing latency and throughput benchmarks leaves rare concurrency bugs hidden in agent-written inference engines, and that human review cannot scale to 1,000 parallel coding agents.

articles.title: Ensuring AI-generated code does what we want
articles.summary: Martin Fowler's site argues that when AI writes both production and test code, customer tests rather than developer tests become the contract between humans and the agent.

articles.title: The Hard Part of AI Coding Is the Second Change
articles.summary: An agent-added retry can double-charge a customer when a timeout hides a successful charge: the feature works, the test suite grows, and the system gets worse.

articles.title: How much of GitHub's most-starred AI tooling is written by coding agents?
articles.summary: Across 324,088 commits in 52 top AI-tooling repos, the median repo has an AI signature on 16.9% of commits from its last 180 active days; 10 repos are at 50% or more.

categories.name: Agent Runtimes: Isolation, Permissions and Shared Resources
categories.summary: Anthropic measured a multi-agent coordination failure, while four open-source projects put controls at the sandbox, the tool call, the MCP config and the prompt.

articles.title: Worse Together: How Performance Breaks Down in Multi-User Multi-Agent Teams
articles.summary: In four simulated environments with models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Alibaba, group outcomes were worse when each user delegated to their own agent than when one agent served everyone.

articles.title: Agent Substrate
articles.summary: A zero-trust sandbox runtime that claims 10x the density of standard containers, resume in under 500ms and more than 500 activations per second, with isolated compute, identity, networking and storage per agent.

articles.title: Show HN: Taster – Plain-English rules your agent can't forget or ignore
articles.summary: Checks every agent tool call against plain-English rules before it runs, and screens each tool result for prompt injection before the agent reads it.

articles.title: Agent-access-review – an access review for AI agents' MCP configs
articles.summary: Inventories an organization's agents and MCP servers, works out what each can read, write, execute and send, and tests that access against 12 controls mapped to NIST 800-53 and SOC 2.

articles.title: Keeping names, emails and phone numbers out of LLM prompts with a local proxy
articles.summary: swapback is a fail-closed local proxy that swaps names, emails, phone numbers and keys for placeholders before a prompt leaves the machine, then restores them in replies, streams and tool calls.

categories.name: Inference Serving: Day-0 Models and New Serving Engines
categories.summary: Google open-sourced two pieces of its serving stack, and vLLM shipped same-day support for two new models with published throughput numbers.

articles.title: Google gooses Python AI performance by... removing Python
articles.summary: Google open-sourced XSE, the XLA Serving Engine, which takes the Python interpreter out of the serving path and handles six million queries a second across Search, Ads and YouTube Shorts.

articles.title: Inkling 2 Small on vLLM: Day-0 Support
articles.summary: vLLM serves Thinking Machines' multimodal MoE model (594B total, 17B active parameters, up to 1M tokens of context) at up to 630 tokens per second per user, with LoRA support.

articles.title: H3-Image Day-0 Support: 4K in 0.87s with Vera Rubin
articles.summary: vLLM-Omni runs MiniMax H3-Image on four NVIDIA Vera Rubin GPUs at a 0.87-second median for native 4096×4096 images; a separate throughput configuration reaches 6,115 images per hour.

articles.title: Google Open-Sources TPU Sync for KV Cache and Weight Transfer on TPUs
articles.summary: Google open-sourced TPU Sync for moving KV cache and model weights on TPUs.

articles.title: Deploy frontier AI models on AWS Trainium with SGLang-Neuron
articles.summary: AWS walks through serving frontier models on its Trainium chips with SGLang-Neuron.

categories.name: Model Churn and What It Does to Your Cost Model
categories.summary: Production models turn over in weeks, a hosted model API is going away, and one team found its discount math was wrong.

articles.title: Vercel Data Shows AI Models Have Six-Week Half-Life in Production
articles.summary: Vercel's November AI Gateway Production Index, drawn from more than 100 trillion tokens a month, puts the effective half-life of a model in production at about six weeks.

articles.title: Our LLM cost model was double-counting batch and cache discounts
articles.summary: Batch is half price on every provider that offers it, yet it is the smallest of three cost levers, does not stack with caching the way it appears to, and loses to a tier drop.

articles.title: Inception's Diffusion LLM API Is Shutting Down
articles.summary: A customer posted an email from Inception Labs saying the Mercury API that hosts its diffusion models is shutting down; no blog post had been published yet.

categories.name: Data Systems Sized for Agent Query Load
categories.summary: Databricks and a new embedded graph engine both redesign the data layer around agents as the caller.

articles.title: Lakehouse//RT: Scale real-time analytics, not your bill
articles.summary: Databricks targets the sustained concurrency of agents, which can run hundreds of queries per second where a human analyst runs a few dozen in an afternoon.

articles.title: Relate by Neo4j – embedded, agent-native graph database
articles.summary: A Rust property-graph engine in a single binary that speaks Cypher 25 and stores a graph as one file, a directory or in memory, with Python, Node.js, WASM and Rust bindings.

articles.title: Genie in Slack is now Generally Available: Governed AI cowork, right where work happens
articles.summary: Generally available: Genie answers in DMs and channels under the asker's Unity Catalog permissions, and updates documents and tickets through MCP connectors after approval.
